objective: put the ported front-end on the operator's machine, and on their screen

what_was_installed.the_package: calix-gpui-git r4874.gaaa19992-1, built from the branch by scripts/install-machine --from-local
what_was_installed.the_binary: /usr/lib/calix/calix-gpui, on gpui-pre 0.3.9 — the port, not the old gpui 0.2.2 branch
what_was_installed.the_framework: the strings of the installed binary carry gpui-pre-0.3.9 and no gpui-0.2.2
what_was_installed.the_services: calix-daemon.service and calix-notify.service are running the new code

the_window.title: Calix — Universal Package Manager
the_window.native_wayland: xwayland: 0 — a Wayland client, not an XWayland one
the_window.how_it_was_seen: read passively from the compositor (hyprctl clients). The pointer was never moved and no input was sent; the operator's focus and pointer are the operator's.

the_path_that_got_there: the tree was already green; the packaging was what failed
the flags makepkg inherits were the cause: -flto=auto broke the link, -C opt-level=3 switched the measurements off, -C target-cpu=native made the binary machine-specific
the package now states its own flags, and the gate holds them (the 'build-flags' step)
scripts/install-machine --from-local built the package from the branch and installed it
the_limitations: The window is up and the compositor knows it; nobody has yet said what it looks like. The audit's limitation — 'a human eye has not looked at the ported application' — is now the operator's to close.
The application was launched from a shell, not from the desktop entry, so the desktop integration (icon, file associations) was not exercised.
